thread:
Arjun: quick gut-check — if a tenant opts into EU-only residency but we’re active/active, what should the fallback look like when EU capacity is saturated?
Vivian: short answer: don’t silently fail-over writes to non-EU. we need a consented downgrade path not an automatic cross-region write. :warning:
Maria: agreed. propose: reads can come from nearest region (with KV cache TTL guarded), writes should queue or return explicit 429 + hint to client. a manual/automated operator path to approve cross-region writes if customer grants emergency consent.
Leo: two practical options: 1) strict-residency mode = reject non-EU writes; 2) soft-residency = enqueue + async flush when region recovers, with a consent toggle to force-write to fallback region. both need clear auditing.
Arjun: what about session/state? many products expect low-latency writes. enqueuing could break UX. is there a hybrid?
Maria: hybrid: allow a local 'session token' that keeps ephemeral state for UX, but persist canonical state only in EU. on forced fallback we mark records with residency-exception tag and audit reason.
Vivian: important: client SDK must be explicit. server-side auto-override is dangerous. SDKs should surface 429 with a structured reason and a CTA to surface consent escalation to admins.
Leo: operationally we need: 1) a ResidencyDecision API that returns {region, allowed_actions, consent_required, failover_hint} so frontends can show proper UI. 2) audit log entries + KMS-wrapped consent tokens.
Arjun: sample routing policy idea:
```json
{"match":{"tenant_residency":"eu"},"policy":{"primary":"eu-west-1","fallback":{"type":"deny_or_queue","queue_name":"eu-fallback-queue"}}}
```
Maria: add field consent_required:true and a ttl for queued writes. also limit queue size and surface backpressure as metrics.
Vivian: metrics to implement: percent of writes blocked-by-residency, avg queue wait, number of forced-consent events, time-to-replay after EU recovery. these map directly to SLOs and runbook thresholds.
Leo: runbook sketch:
- detect sustained >90% EU capacity for 2m -> post alert
- automatically enable read-only fallback after 5m if admin-approved? (need legal sign-off)
- if no consent and queue > 5000 items -> circuit-break (reject new writes)
ops-bot: deploy requested: residency-guard v0.1 -> canary eu-west-1 (link: https://deploys/internal/2401234567) :white_check_mark:
Arjun: rollout plan: canary in eu with synthetic tenants, then opt-in alpha customers, then broad. we also need a compliance review for consent flow text.
Maria: open questions: how do we surface downstream consistency expectations to clients? e.g., are queued writes visible to reads from other regions? recommend they are not. document that queued writes are eventual and may be invisible until replay.
Vivian: agree. make it explicit in SDK: read-after-write not guaranteed when queued. customers will need to handle optimistic UI or block until commit.
Leo: last: automation for post-failover cleanup — when we replay queued writes, we must detect conflicts and either merge or escalate. we should mark those events in the audit log and expose a reconciliation dashboard.
Arjun: OK action items: @Vivian draft ResidencyDecision API spec + SDk error contract (due EOD friday), @Maria write enqueue semantics + queue sizing proposal, @Leo ops runbook + metrics list, I'll coordinate compliance text.
Vivian: ack. starting a short RFC PR and will drop the link here when ready.
Maria: i'll stub the queue behavior in the simulator so we can run load tests.
Leo: prepping dashboards.
ops-bot: reminder: weekly-architecture-sync in 1h (https://calendar/internal/arch-sync)
Arjun: thanks all — keeping this thread for RFC followup. :thumbsup:
